nodes.name: Dual W-embedding pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: RuW/W–NC was prepared via a facile pyrolysis of self-assembled precursors, including a mixture of dicyandiamide, trimesic acid, ammonium tungstate and ruthenium(III) chloride under an argon atmosphere (see the Methods for details and Fig. S1).
nodes.source_text: RuW/W–NC was prepared via a facile pyrolysis of self-assembled precursors, including a mixture of dicyandiamide, trimesic acid, ammonium tungstate and ruthenium(III) chloride under an argon atmosphere (see the Methods for details and Fig. S1).

nodes.name: Ru/NC pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: Ru/NC was synthesized using a similar method without addition of ammonium tungstate.
nodes.source_text: Ru/NC and W–NC were synthesized using a similar method without addition of specific metal precursors.

nodes.name: W–NC pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: W–NC was synthesized using a similar method without addition of ruthenium(III) chloride.
nodes.source_text: Ru/NC and W–NC were synthesized using a similar method without addition of specific metal precursors.

nodes.description: HOR performance in RDE configuration in 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The HOR performance of RuW/W–NC was initially examined using a standard three-electrode RDE configuration in 0.1 M KOH... RuW/W–NC delivers an exceptional HOR mass activity of 14.09 A mg_Ru⁻¹ in a rotating disk electrode (RDE)
the RuW/W–NC-based AEMFC enables an exceptional peak power density of 2.03 W cm⁻² and an excellent current density of 2.50 A cm⁻² at 0.65 V (J@0.65 V) with a low Ru loading of 0.1 mg_Ru cm⁻² in H₂-O₂
the RuW/W–NC-based AEMFC with a low Ru loading of 0.1 mg cm⁻² delivers a remarkable PPD of 1.44 W cm⁻² in H₂–air

we further reduced the total PGM loading of AEMFCs to 0.125 mg cm⁻² (anode: 0.025 mg_Ru cm⁻², cathode: 0.1 mg_Pt cm⁻²), and the RuW/W–NC-based AEMFC achieved a high PPD of 1.01 W cm⁻² in H₂–air (CO₂ free). The PPD normalized by the total PGM loading is determined to be 8.08 W mg_PGM⁻¹. Additionally, the rated power density reaches 0.91 W cm⁻² at 0.65 V
the RuW/W–NC-based AEMFC can be run stably at a high current density of 1.0 A cm⁻² for over 100 h
RuW/W–NC exhibits a minimal decline in the limiting current density for the HOR in the presence of 1000 ppm CO, and only 17.2% of HOR current decays after 10 000 s
the RuW/W–NC-based AEMFC still achieves a remarkable PPD of 1.29 W cm⁻² in CO/H₂–O₂

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA shows Ru content of 9.8 wt% and W content of 18.0 wt% in RuW/W–NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and EDS demonstrate that the amount of Ru and W in RuW/W–NC is 9.8 and 18.0 wt%, respectively (Fig. S2 and S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Low-magnification HAADF-STEM shows high densities of uniformly distributed Ru nanoclusters averaging 1.65 nm in RuW/W–NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The low-magnification high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images clearly show high densities of uniformly distributed Ru nanoclusters (Fig. 1b and Fig. S6) with an average size of 1.65 nm (Fig. S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of RuW/W–NC shows metallic Ru diffraction peaks with Ru(101) shifted to lower angle compared to Ru/NC; no crystalline W phases observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of RuW/W–NC shows a characteristic diffraction peak corresponding to metallic Ru, while no crystalline phases associated with W are observed (Fig. 1g), suggesting the presence of atomically dispersed W single atoms on the NC support. In addition, compared to Ru/NC, the XRD peaks of Ru (101) in RuW/W–NC shift to a lower degree.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows Ru–Ru lattice fringe spacing of 2.16 Å in RuW/W–NC (vs 2.05 Å in Ru/NC), corresponding to mean tensile strain of 5.4%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM and the corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) images of RuW/W–NC demonstrate that the spacing of the Ru–Ru lattice fringe in RuW/W–NC is stretched to 2.16 Å compared to the spacing in Ru/NC (2.05 Å) (Fig. 1h)... The mean tensile strain of RuW/W–NC was calculated to be approximately 5.4%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES confirms Ru in RuW/W–NC exists mainly in metallic state, close to Ru foil with lower white line intensity than RuO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the normalized X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) of the Ru K-edge, the oxidation state of RuW/W–NC is close to that of Ru foil, and the intensity of the white line peak is significantly lower than that in RuO2, confirming that Ru mainly exists in a metallic state in RuW/W–NC (Fig. 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ru–W/Ru bond at 2.4 Å in RuW/W–NC (vs Ru–Ru at 2.3 Å in Ru/NC); W L3-edge FT-EXAFS shows W–NC at 1.4 Å and W–W shifted to 2.5 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra (Fig. 2c), the bond length of Ru–W/Ru (2.4 Å) in RuW/W–NC is larger than that of Ru–Ru (2.3 Å) in Ru/NC... the peak at around 1.4 Å corresponding to the W–NC coordination can be found in the W L3-edge FT-EXAFS of RuW/W–NC and W–NC... the W–W bond in RuW/W–NC negatively shifts to 2.5 Å compared to 2.7 Å in the W foil.
